parts.text: Regenerate the truth-reader implementation from the prior array-projection design with this additional requirement as authoritative. Do NOT rebuild or rewrite an unseeded reader projection merely because the repository HEAD changed. Each canonical source document must have per-document reader provenance recording the exact source revision used to build that reader. Use source-specific provenance, not global HEAD: record at minimum the canonical source blob SHA and the last commit SHA that changed that source path (for example git rev-parse HEAD:<source_path> plus git log -1 --format=%H -- <source_path>). Before a selected document is challenged, compare the current canonical source provenance against the stored reader provenance. If both match, reuse the existing unseeded reader projection without regenerating it. If either differs, regenerate that reader mechanically from the COMPLETE current canonical source, preserve all content/order under the existing ordered-array projection rules, then update its provenance. Unrelated repository commits must not cause reader regeneration. Separate the stable unseeded reader from the ephemeral seeded challenge projection: the stable reader changes only when its canonical source provenance changes; the active seeded projection may be recreated/updated each challenge from that stable reader. Seeds remain separate array elements inserted at deterministic coverage intervals, including near the beginning and end. The worker returns every seed in active projection order; exact complete ordered match is required for truth PASS. Keep enumerated selector booleans, workflow-only Node authority, CSPRNG seeds, separate evidence file, zero mutation on FAIL, and atomic PASS cleanup. On PASS clear/reset active seeded projections/evidence/selector state without rewriting unchanged stable readers. Return response_type truth_reader_implementation with files[] containing exact repository paths and COMPLETE contents for the revised Node engine, workflow, selector/evidence/catalog/status/provenance surfaces, and any reader/active projection files required.
